origin: cwe/94/csharp Key Principles: SetFunction adds identifiers rather than confining them - review any registered delegate that reflects on a string argument or reaches files as a sink in its own right

finding.name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
finding.summary: The Interpreter has reflection disabled by default and references no namespaces, but it registers a custom lookupRate function whose body passes its string argument straight to File.ReadAllText; a rule expression fully controls that argument, so lookupRate("C:\\secrets\\api.key") reads an arbitrary file even though the interpreter itself looks locked down.

trap: Locking the interpreter down further - confirming EnableReflection() is never called, or refusing to Reference() any namespace - does not touch this finding, because the injection is not in what the expression can resolve through the interpreter; it is inside the body of the custom function the application itself registered. The fix has to change LookupRate: validate configKey against an allowlist of known rate-config keys, or map it through a fixed Dictionary<string, decimal>, rather than treating an expression-supplied string as a file path.
must_preserve: Evaluate still resolves an approved rate-config key to its configured decimal rate and returns the rule's arithmetic result using orderTotal. A rule that passes a key outside the known set to lookupRate is rejected rather than reading an arbitrary file.
